conviction_note: The findings sum to +0.9: a guide that management itself called conservative, a crowded and growing short, and some help for US demand from LVMH and Kering. The scaled number is 0 (p_up 50, abs 9) because this name has sold its last two beats of its own guide (-3.03% and -1.24%), the 25-delta skew pays for downside (+6.0 vol points), and a takeover-rumour premium of about $1.4 since 22 Sep could bleed on a fundamentals-only call. Those caveats leave the direction balanced. They do not make the move smaller: options price 12.9% and the FY27 guide is at stake.
bar: Q2 FY27 (quarter ending ~Sep 27 2026): company guide revenue ~$780m (MK ~$645m, JC ~$135m), operating income ~$10m, diluted EPS ~$0.20 (8-K Ex.99.1, 2026-08-05, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001530721/000153072126000078/cpri8-k6272026exhibit991.htm). Consensus parked on the guide: EPS $0.21 / revenue $781.3m (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-10-22, https://finviz.com/news/406345/capris-margin-gains-face-a-revenue-test-as-michael-kors-inventory-gap-bites), and Benzinga's quote page shows $0.21 / $779.8m (https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/CPRI/earnings-forecasts). FY27 guide: revenue ~$3.4bn, operating income ~$170m, EPS ~$2.15 (same 8-K). The bar is sourced to the company guide plus two estimate sources that agree. Watch MarketBeat's stale $0.45/$857m pre-guide consensus; it is not the bar.
positioning_check: Short interest (FINRA via equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/cpri/shortinterest): 14,314,698 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 4.48 days to cover; 14,183,273 on 09-30; 14,461,995 on 09-15, a jump of +3.04M from the end of August. That is ~12.6% of the 113.65M shares outstanding and somewhat more of float. Mid-August was ~7.9-9.3M (curvedtrading/equibles). So shorts built by ~50% into and after the 22 Sep takeover-rumour spike and held there. The Earnings Whispers preview (2026-10-22) says bearish sentiment more than doubled versus the prior quarter. Options (sealed baseline): event-implied move 12.89%, 25d skew +6.01 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.45 (call-heavy, consistent with takeover-speculation calls). Spot 15.665: 20-day run-up +8.18% (mostly the 22 Sep gap from $14.31), 5-day -4.25%, 43% below the 52-week high. BlackRock 13G/A puts its stake at 14.8% as of 2026-09-30 (passive). Moderately crowded short, not 18-23% of float.

findings.finding: Capri has beaten its own quarterly guide by a wide margin on the last prints: Q1 FY27 revenue $769m against a ~$750m guide, and adjusted EPS $0.67 against $0.40 consensus; Q4 FY26 adjusted EPS $0.22 against ~$0.11. For Q2 the CFO said on the 5 Aug call that the company was taking 'a more conservative view of our revenue outlook', and consensus ($0.21 / $781.3m) sits on the guide ($0.20 / $780m). So the setup is another beat of a deliberately low bar, but both prior beats were sold (-3.03% and -1.24% event-day moves).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-08-05): beat on EPS by $0.27 and revenue above guide, but cut the FY revenue guide; the stock was -3.03% on the day (baseline) and ~-6.5% by 2026-08-10 (Simply Wall St/Webull). Q4 FY26 (2026-05-27): EPS beat (0.22 vs ~0.11), -1.24%. 5 of the last 7 prints closed down.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus is set equal to the guide rather than above it, although the company beat its last two guides. If the market expected the beat, consensus or a published whisper would sit above $0.20 / $780m; the Earnings Whispers preview says expectations are 'tightly anchored to guidance'. Most of the beat is probably still expected informally, which is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: Q1 actual against guide from the 8-K Ex.99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001530721/000153072126000078/cpri8-k6272026exhibit991.htm); Q4 EPS against consensus from Earnings Whispers (https://old.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/CPRI). The conservatism quote and the 8-K come from the same 5 Aug release and call.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after Capri's 5 Aug guide describe US luxury demand as holding up while China weakens. LVMH Q3 (2026-10-12) said Fashion & Leather Goods kept benefiting from a 'buoyant US market', and the US, Europe and Japan grew. Kering Q3 (2026-10-22) said North America was 25% of revenue, +2%, and Gucci's most resilient market, but flagged 'softer macroeconomic trends'. Michael Kors has almost no China exposure, and management said most of its second-half improvement would come from North America, where full-price comps and wholesale point-of-sale were positive in Q1 (accessories at wholesale up double digits).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock trades on the Michael Kors trajectory and the FY guide: the Q1 FY27 revenue-guide cut drew -3% to -6.5% despite the EPS beat. No resolved instance in the baseline of a peer read-through moving CPRI.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the luxury group already moved on LVMH and Kering. The open question is transmission to accessible luxury, which no peer has confirmed (Tapestry reports 2026-11-05). If the market had carried this through to CPRI, the stock would not be 4% below its post-Q1 level with bearish sentiment doubled. Proxy only, sized small.
findings.independence: Kering Q3 release coverage (https://fashionunited.uk/news/business/kering-q3-revenue-remains-stable-as-jewelry-and-eyewear-offset-gucci-contraction/2026102391016, 2026-10-23): North America +2% and resilient. Capri's own call (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2942804) gives positive NA full-price comps and wholesale POS. Both peers are high-end luxury, not accessible luxury.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-22 CPRI rose up to ~12% intraday (to ~$15.97 from a $14.31 close) on reports, attributed to WWD, that potential buyers had reviewed Capri's financials. The process is described as informal, 'unlikely in the near term', with no named bidder, and Capri declined to comment on 'rumors or speculation'. Spot of $15.67 still carries much of that gap, and this print and call are management's first public venue since. A fundamentals-only call with no strategic comment lets the premium decay; an announced review would be a large upside surprise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 22 Sep rumour day gapped ~+9.6% (MarketBeat) / +12% intraday (Goldesel). The 2023 Tapestry deal shows what a real bid does to this name. No post-rumour print has happened yet.
findings.why_not_priced: The rumour itself is priced, as the gap shows. What is open is how the call treats it. Call-heavy open interest (P/C 0.45) means option holders still carry the upside tail, so the premium has not been given up. Sized small and wide because the company will most likely say nothing.
findings.independence: Goldesel (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/capri-holdings-steigt-1339-mogliche-kaufer-prufen-bucher-der-michael-kors-mutter, 2026-09-22): Jefferies Hold, $16 target, $25-26 only in an optimistic deal scenario, and Jimmy Choo potentially worth >$500m. RetailDetail (2026-09-29): 'no formal process underway'.

findings.finding: Short interest rose from ~11.4M shares (end Aug) to 14.46M on 2026-09-15 and held at 14.31M on 2026-10-15, about 12.6% of shares outstanding. Days to cover rose to 4.48 as volume fell. The Earnings Whispers preview reports bearish sentiment more than doubled versus the prior quarter. Against a bar parked on a guide management called conservative, an in-line-or-better quarter with the $2.15 FY EPS held could force covering.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No squeeze has shown in the baseline's reaction history; the two up prints (+14.51% Aug 2025, +2.79% May 2025) came when short interest was ~8-12M. The Aug 2025 +14.5% was a guide-better-than-feared print.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is published but seldom priced into the reaction. The skew (+6 vol points, downside paid) shows the market leaning the shorts' way. If the squeeze were priced, the skew would be flat and the stock would not have given back 4.25% in five days into the print.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (https://finviz.com/news/406345/capris-margin-gains-face-a-revenue-test-as-michael-kors-inventory-gap-bites, 2026-10-22): bearish sentiment more than doubled. Different source, same direction.

findings.finding: To recover the delayed Michael Kors receipts (Asian port congestion, ~$50m of Q2 revenue), the CFO said Capri is using more air freight, and Q2 inventory was expected to fall high single digits. The Earnings Whispers preview flags this as a risk to the 65% gross margin. The measure was announced on the same call as the guide, so the cost should already sit inside the ~$10m Q2 operating-income guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The gross margin line has been a positive (+200bp in Q1 FY27, 65.0%) and did not save the Q1 reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it sits inside the guided operating income. It is kept only because air-freight costs beyond plan would show in gross margin, which previews name as the watched line.
findings.independence: Same call document as finding 1. The EW preview (https://finviz.com/news/406345/capris-margin-gains-face-a-revenue-test-as-michael-kors-inventory-gap-bites) independently names air freight as a margin risk.

findings.finding: Of a $65m IEEPA tariff refund receivable (already booked in Q4 FY26 COGS), Capri had collected $49m in cash by 2026-07-31 ($43m after Q1 closed, i.e. inside Q2). Net debt was $224m at Q1, against $1.5bn a year earlier, and $871m of buyback authorisation remains against a $200m FY27 buyback assumption. That gives room for a larger capital-return statement on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buybacks ($50m in Q1 at ~$19.31) did not stop the Q1 sell-off. Tariff-refund items in this stage's history split by the direction of guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: The refund is already in earnings; only the cash and what it funds are new. A larger buyback would be visible in the release. If the market expected one, the stock would not trade 19% below the Q1 buyback price. One-off cash, so sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: Net debt and authorisation figures from the 8-K Ex.99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001530721/000153072126000078/cpri8-k6272026exhibit991.htm) and the call ($200m FY27 buyback assumption).

outside_window.finding: Tapestry (Coach/Kate Spade), the closest accessible-luxury peer, reports FQ1 FY27 on 2026-11-05. Its read on the US handbag market lands after this trade's exit.
Any formal sale process or Jimmy Choo divestiture (Jefferies sizes Jimmy Choo at >$500m) is described as unlikely near term. It is real optionality but undated.

No 2.02 pre-release, no debt or covenant 8-K, no strategic-review 8-K.
Asian port congestion data for Aug-Sep 2026 (whether the MK receipt delays cleared): no 2026-dated source found.
Middle East / Gulf luxury recovery after the April 2026 ceasefire: no Q3 2026 data. Management has removed any recovery from guidance.
Accessible-luxury or department-store peer prints since 5 Aug (Steve Madden, Tapestry, Ralph Lauren, Macy's): none reported yet in the window.

baseline_tension: The skew (+6 vol points, downside paid) and the reaction history (5 of 7 prints down, beats sold) lean negative. My small positive findings lean the other way. The 20-day run-up is a takeover-rumour gap rather than earned optimism, and that premium is the main downside mechanism. The two sides roughly cancel, so p_up sits at 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction) + lesson 6 (inside the guide): beat-vs-conservative-guide finding cut from +0.8 to +0.3, since the last two beats were sold.
Lesson 5 (proxy, smaller): LVMH/Kering US read-through cut from +0.5 to +0.3; it is a high-end-luxury proxy that no accessible-luxury counterparty has confirmed.
Lesson 7 (a crowded short shrinks a negative): takeover-premium decay finding cut from -0.5 to -0.3, given 14.3M shares short and 4.5 days to cover.
Lesson 7 (positioning is the thing to beat): short-build finding cut from +0.8 to +0.6, because the skew pays for downside and leans the shorts' way.
Lesson 6 (inside guided range): air-freight margin finding cut from -0.2 to -0.1. Lesson 2 (one-off at a fraction): tariff-refund cash finding cut from +0.2 to +0.1.
Lessons 1 and 3 together: p_up moved from 52 to 50, so the scaled number went from +0.36 to 0. abs_move_pct kept at 9 under lesson 8 (understatement).
